persona-5-royal: By day you're a transfer student in Tokyo, juggling classes, part-time jobs and friendships. By night you and your friends become the Phantom Thieves, slipping into the twisted inner worlds of corrupt adults to steal their hearts. It's a long, stylish, turn-based RPG with one of the best soundtracks around, and Royal is the expanded version with a whole extra semester.
god-of-war: Kratos leaves Greek myth behind for the Norse wilds, where he sets out with his young son Atreus to scatter his wife's ashes from the highest peak. The axe combat is heavy and satisfying, and the story of a hard father learning to raise his kid gives it real weight. Start here before Ragnarök.
god-of-war-ragnarok: The sequel picks up a few years later as Fimbulwinter grips the world and Ragnarök draws near. It's bigger in every way, with more realms, more ways to fight and a larger cast, but it still comes back to Kratos and Atreus.
the-last-of-us-part-ii-remastered: Five years after the first game, Ellie sets out across a ruined Seattle on a quest for revenge, and the story asks hard questions about what that costs. The tense stealth and scavenging are some of the best in the genre, but it's a heavy, violent story. The PS5 version adds No Return, a replayable survival mode.
uncharted-4-a-thief-s-end: Nathan Drake is pulled out of retirement by the brother he thought was dead, for one last hunt after a legendary pirate treasure. It's a blockbuster adventure of climbing, gunfights and set pieces, with warm, funny characters holding it together.
bloodborne: FromSoftware's gothic nightmare sends you through the plague-ridden city of Yharnam, hunting beasts that get stranger the deeper you go. The combat is fast and rewards aggression rather than hiding behind a shield. It's hard and makes no apologies, but few games feel this rewarding once it clicks, and it's a PlayStation exclusive.
blue-prince: You've inherited a mansion whose rooms rearrange every day, and you pick each new room from a hand of options as you open each door, looking for the rumoured 46th room. It's a puzzle game full of clues, codes and secrets that keeps surprising you long after the credits.
demon-s-souls: A ground-up PS5 remake of the 2009 game that started the Souls series, from the team at Bluepoint. You fight through the cursed kingdom of Boletaria, one dangerous level at a time. It looks stunning and is a gentler way into FromSoftware's style than Bloodborne, though only just.
rayman-legends: A bright, inventive 2D platformer that's easy to pick up and great with up to four players on one couch. The musical levels, where you run and jump in time with the soundtrack, are the highlight.
undertale: A small RPG with a big reputation. You fall into an underground world of monsters, and you can talk your way out of every fight instead of winning it. It's funny, strange and surprisingly moving, and the choices you make change how it all plays out.
overcooked-all-you-can-eat: Chaotic kitchen co-op where you chop, cook and serve against the clock in kitchens that split apart, slide around or catch fire. It's simple enough for anyone to pick up and guaranteed to have you shouting at each other within minutes. This edition bundles both games and all their extra content.
sackboy-a-big-adventure: A cheerful, inventive 3D platformer starring the knitted hero from LittleBigPlanet. Some levels can only be reached together, and the music levels set to pop songs are a joy. A great pick for families.
terraria: Dig, build, explore and fight your way through a huge 2D world that keeps surprising you with bosses, biomes and secrets. Split-screen lets everyone go their own way, then regroup to take on the next boss together.
untitled-goose-game: You're a horrible goose, and the village is your playground: steal hats, ruin picnics and honk at everyone. The two-player mode lets a second goose join the mischief, which makes it twice as funny. Short, silly and perfect for a lazy afternoon.
vampire-survivors: You walk, the weapons fire on their own, and within minutes the screen fills with thousands of monsters and dazzling attacks. It's very hard to stop playing, and even better with friends on the same sofa.
trine-4-the-nightmare-prince: A gorgeous fairy-tale puzzle platformer where a wizard, a knight and a thief combine their skills to get past each obstacle. With friends, every puzzle turns into a creative argument about the best way through.
children-of-morta: A hand-drawn action RPG about a family of heroes defending their mountain home, with each family member playing differently. A second player can jump in as another member of the family, and the story is surprisingly moving.
lego-city-undercover: A funny open-world LEGO adventure where you play an undercover cop in a city full of jokes and secrets. The split-screen co-op makes it one of the best ways to play with younger kids.
human-fall-flat: A physics puzzle game where you control a wobbly, floppy character through dream-like levels. Solving things is hard, and failing is hilarious, especially with a friend grabbing onto you at the worst possible moment.
helldivers-2: You and up to three friends drop onto alien planets to spread "managed democracy", completing objectives while bugs and robots swarm in from every direction. Friendly fire is always on, which is half the fun, and every mission feeds into a galaxy-wide war that the whole community fights together.
warhammer-40-000-space-marine-2: A loud, brutal third-person shooter where you and two friends take on endless tides of alien Tyranids as towering Space Marines. The whole campaign can be played in co-op, and the separate Operations missions are built for a full squad.
ghost-of-tsushima-director-s-cut: The main game is a single-player samurai epic, but it also includes Legends, a free co-op mode drawn from Japanese folklore. You pick a class, team up with friends and fight through story missions, survival waves and a full raid.
abiotic-factor: A survival crafting game set in a secret underground research lab where everything has gone wrong. You and your friends are scientists, not soldiers, so you scavenge, build and science your way past monsters from other dimensions. It's funny, clever and much better with a group.
nioh: A tough samurai action game set in a fantasy version of feudal Japan, full of demons and deep, precise combat. Calling in a friend to help with a boss that's been beating you for an hour is one of its great pleasures.
tetris-effect-connected: Tetris at its most beautiful, with music and visuals that react to every move. The Connected mode lets three players combine their boards to take down a boss together, which is unlike any Tetris you've played.
warhammer-vermintide-2: A first-person action game where four heroes hold the line against hordes of rat-men and Chaos warriors. Its satisfying melee combat and teamwork-heavy missions have kept a loyal crowd playing for years.
far-cry-5: A cult has taken over a corner of rural Montana, and you're there to take it back. The whole open-world campaign can be played with a friend, which turns its explosive, unpredictable fights into a great night of shared chaos.
tom-clancy-s-the-division-2: A cover-based shooter with loot, set in a Washington, D.C. falling apart after a pandemic. Taking back the city block by block with a full squad is where it shines, and there's a huge amount to do.
dying-light-2-stay-human: Run, climb and leap across the rooftops of a zombie-infested city, and stay off the streets after dark. The parkour feels great on its own and even better racing friends across the skyline.
celeste: Madeline sets out to climb Celeste Mountain, and you guide her through hundreds of tight, inventive platforming screens. It's hard but always fair, with instant restarts and an Assist Mode if you need it. Underneath the jumping is a warm, honest story about anxiety and self-doubt.
shadow-of-the-colossus: A lone hero rides across a vast, empty land to topple sixteen giant colossi, each one a living puzzle you have to climb. This is Bluepoint's beautiful PS4 remake of the PS2 classic, and it still has one of the most haunting endings in games.
sword-of-the-sea: From the makers of Abzû and Journey's art director: you surf across sweeping desert dunes on a hovering sword, bringing a lost sea back to life as you go. It's pure, flowing movement with gorgeous art and music, and you'll want to play it again right away.
neva: A young woman named Alba and a wolf cub named Neva travel together through a dying, painterly world over the course of the seasons. It's from the team behind GRIS, mixing gentle platforming with tense fights and a wordless story about growing up.
indika: Indika is a young nun in a strange, alternate 19th-century Russia, and the Devil himself is a voice in her head. Sent on an errand across a frozen landscape, she falls in with an escaped convict, and what follows is a darkly funny, often surreal story about faith and doubt. It's like nothing else on the service.
hotline-miami: A brutal, neon-soaked top-down action game set in 1989 Miami, where you clear out buildings in a single blur of violence and die in one hit. Its pounding synth soundtrack and "one more try" loop make it hard to put down. Very violent, so not one for the kids.
gris: A wordless journey through a watercolour world that slowly gains colour as a young woman works through her grief. There's no way to fail, just gentle platforming, stunning art and music. Perfect for a quiet evening.
venba: A short, heartfelt story about an Indian family who move to Canada in the 1980s, told through cooking. You piece together the mother's recipes from a smudged old cookbook, and each dish carries a memory. You can finish it in one sitting.
bramble-the-mountain-king: A young boy follows his sister into a forest straight out of Nordic folklore, where the fairy-tale creatures are anything but friendly. It begins beautiful and turns very dark, with some genuinely grim moments and memorable boss fights, so it's one for older players.
resident-evil-village: Ethan Winters searches a snowbound European village for his kidnapped daughter, and runs into a castle of vampires, beasts in the woods and much worse. Some stretches are more action than horror, but the ones that go for scares are pure nightmare fuel, above all a certain house in the hills.
the-evil-within-2: Detective Sebastian Castellanos plugs back into STEM, a shared nightmare world, to find his daughter in a small town that's tearing itself apart. It pairs tense stealth and scarce ammo with grotesque monsters and a few unforgettable villains, and its open areas let you choose how much danger to walk into.
outlast-2: A journalist searching for his wife in the Arizona desert stumbles into a murderous cult, armed with nothing but a camcorder and its night vision. You can't fight back, only run and hide, and it never lets up. It's also extremely graphic, so it's strictly for adults.
until-dawn-2015: Eight friends spend a night in a remote mountain lodge, and something is hunting them. Every choice you make can save a character or get them killed, so it's built to be replayed. It's like starring in your own slasher movie, and it's great fun with friends calling out the choices.
still-wakes-the-deep: It's 1975 on an oil rig in the North Sea, and something has come up from below. You're an ordinary electrician with no weapons, just a desperate need to get home. The strong Scottish voice acting and the storm-battered rig make it hugely atmospheric.
crow-country: It's 1990, and you're investigating an abandoned theme park with a dark secret. Crow Country is a loving tribute to the PS1 survival horror classics, with puzzles, limited ammo and creepy low-poly visuals, but it's far friendlier than the games it imitates.
metro-exodus: Artyom and his comrades flee the tunnels under Moscow on a steam train, crossing a ruined Russia full of mutants, bandits and things lurking in the dark. Between its open areas come tight, claustrophobic stretches where your gas mask filter and a flickering light are all that stand between you and something horrible.
call-of-cthulhu: In 1924, a private investigator travels to a remote island off the New England coast to look into a painter's mysterious death. The deeper he digs into the island's secrets, the more his grip on reality slips. It's rough around the edges, but its creeping Lovecraftian dread is the real thing.
killer-frequency: You're a late-night radio DJ in a small 1980s town, and the emergency line has been rerouted to your booth just as a masked killer starts picking off the locals. You help callers survive over the phone, in a game that's as funny as it is tense.
